cut30Scenes.subtitle: NOV 18, 2026 // ONE LIGHT DAY MILESTONE
cut30Scenes.headline: A Text That Takes 24 Hours to Arrive
cut30Scenes.metricSub: Light travels 299,792 km/s. On Nov 18, 2026 at 02:16 PST, Voyager 1 reaches 24 light hours from Earth.
cut30Scenes.summary: Forty nine years after launch, humanity's farthest spacecraft is still not a single light year away. On November 18, 2026, it reaches one light day, answering Earth with a 22 watt refrigerator bulb radio.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: On November 18, 2026, a radio signal to Voyager 1 takes twenty four hours to arrive. NASA's left behind hardware is still teaching us.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: STOP 1: THE MOON // PASSIVE LASER RETROREFLECTORS
cut30Scenes.headline: The Mirror on the Moon With Zero Batteries
cut30Scenes.metricSub: One way laser travel is 1.28s (2.56s round trip), proving the Moon has a fluid core and recedes at fingernail growth speed.
cut30Scenes.summary: Apollo astronauts left unpowered glass prisms in the lunar dust over fifty years ago. Fire a laser from Earth today, and those mirrors still bounce the light back in 2.56 seconds.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: In our interactive experience, students bounce lasers off unpowered Moon mirrors that prove the Moon drifts away at 3.8 centimeters a year.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: STOP 2 & 3: MARS TELEMETRY & TITAN SLINGSHOT
cut30Scenes.headline: Why NASA Gave Up Pluto for an Orange Moon
cut30Scenes.metricSub: At Saturn on Nov 12, 1980 (1.52B km from Earth), skimming Titan traded a Pluto visit for interstellar space.
cut30Scenes.summary: Mars rovers fought dust storms until their solar panels went dark. At Saturn, NASA sacrificed a visit to Pluto so Voyager 1 could dive under Titan's orange smog and fling itself toward the stars.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: Readers uncover the real telemetry behind Opportunity's final storm on Mars, and trace Voyager 1's gravity slingshot past Saturn and Titan.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: INTERSTELLAR LEGACY // LEFT BEHIND, STILL TEACHING US
cut30Scenes.headline: Everything We Ever Knew Inside a Single Pixel
cut30Scenes.metricSub: With two sensors active in late 2026 and the Golden Record aboard, Voyager 1 will outlast the stars themselves.
cut30Scenes.summary: Thirty four minutes after photographing Earth as a tiny blue speck inside a sunbeam, Voyager 1 turned its cameras off forever. Every silent machine left in space paid the price for the discoveries that came home.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: Every machine that stayed behind paid the price for the knowledge that came home. Left behind. Still teaching us.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: NOVEMBER 18, 2026 // 02:16 PST MILESTONE
cut30Scenes.headline: The Light Year Myth vs. The 22 Watt Refrigerator Bulb
cut30Scenes.metricSub: At 299,792.458 km/s, light covers 25.902 billion km in 24 hours. Reaching 1 light year will take nearly 18,000 years.
cut30Scenes.summary: People assume our farthest probe has traveled several light years, yet it has covered less than one percent of one. On November 18, 2026, Voyager 1 reaches one light day, whispering across a 48 hour round trip with a 22 watt bulb.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: Send a radio command to Voyager 1 on November 18, 2026, and that signal takes twenty four hours to arrive. After forty nine years of flight, humanity's farthest probe is reaching one full light day from Earth using a twenty two watt refrigerator bulb transmitter.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: SEPT 18, 1977 // THE TORCH PASSED IN THE DARK
cut30Scenes.headline: A Once in 176 Year Slingshot & A Golden Time Capsule
cut30Scenes.metricSub: On Sept 18, 1977, from 11.66M km away (38.9s light delay), Voyager 1 took the first single frame photo of Earth and the Moon.
cut30Scenes.summary: When human Moon landings ended in 1972, twin robotic scouts took the torch. Riding a planetary alignment that happens once every 176 years, they looked back to photograph Earth and the Moon together while carrying a Golden Record.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: Five years after Apollo 17 splashed down, NASA launched the twin Voyagers in 1977 to ride a once in 176 year planetary alignment. Two weeks out, Voyager 1 captured the first single frame portrait of Earth and the Moon, carrying a Golden Record built to outlast civilization.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: MARCH 5, 1979 // JUPITER & LINDA MORABITO'S DISCOVERY
cut30Scenes.headline: The Late Night Photo That Proved Alien Worlds Are Alive
cut30Scenes.metricSub: On March 5, 1979, Jupiter stood 678.4M km from Earth (37m 43s light time) as Voyager 1 returned 19,000 photographs.
cut30Scenes.summary: Voyager 1 braved Jupiter's lethal radiation belts to steal orbital speed toward Saturn. Three nights later, navigation engineer Linda Morabito brightened a routine crescent photo of Io and caught a 300 kilometer volcano erupting into space.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: In March 1979, six hundred seventy eight million kilometers from Earth, Voyager 1 braved Jupiter's radiation belts to steal orbital speed. Three days later, engineer Linda Morabito brightened a navigation photo of the moon Io and discovered a 300 kilometer volcanic plume erupting into space.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: NOVEMBER 12, 1980 // THE SACRIFICE AT SATURN
cut30Scenes.headline: Trading Pluto Forever for the Orange Haze of Titan
cut30Scenes.metricSub: At Saturn encounter (1.52B km from Earth, 1h 24m 30s light delay), Titan's gravity bent Voyager 1's path 35 degrees northward.
cut30Scenes.summary: At Saturn, engineers faced an irreversible choice: fly straight ahead to Pluto, or dive beneath the orange moon Titan. Choosing Titan unlocked its thick prebiotic air, while its gravity flung Voyager 1 upward out of the planetary plane forever.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: At Saturn in November 1980, one point five billion kilometers from home, engineers faced a permanent trade: steer straight to Pluto, or dive beneath the orange moon Titan. Choosing Titan unlocked its thick prebiotic atmosphere, while slinging Voyager 1 upward out of the planetary plane forever.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: AUG 25, 1989 // THE CRIPPLED TWIN THAT KEPT GOING
cut30Scenes.headline: Half Deaf on a Backup Radio at Uranus & Neptune
cut30Scenes.metricSub: At Neptune on Aug 25, 1989 (4.426B km from Earth, 4h 06m 04s light delay), Triton's nitrogen geysers rose 8 km high.
cut30Scenes.summary: Listening on a single backup radio receiver, Voyager 2 visited sideways Uranus and windswept Neptune all alone. Arriving within one second of schedule after twelve years in flight, it caught nitrogen geysers erupting on frozen Triton.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: While Voyager 1 climbed above the planets, its half deaf twin Voyager 2 carried the torch alone to Uranus and Neptune. Arriving four point four billion kilometers away within one second of schedule, it caught nitrogen geysers shooting eight kilometers high on frozen Triton.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: AUG 25, 2012 // PALE BLUE DOT & INTERSTELLAR CROSSING
cut30Scenes.headline: Thirty Four Minutes to Blindness & The Ringing Galaxy
cut30Scenes.metricSub: Crossed the heliopause at 18.115B km (16h 47m 05s light time), confirmed in April 2013 when a solar wave vibrated interstellar gas.
cut30Scenes.summary: On Valentine's Day 1990, Voyager 1 captured Earth as a tiny blue pixel inside a sunbeam just 34 minutes before turning its cameras off forever. In April 2013, a solar storm made surrounding gas ring like a violin string, proving it had entered interstellar space.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: After photographing Earth as a single pixel on Valentine's Day 1990, Voyager 1 powered down its cameras forever to save heat. In April 2013, a solar storm made surrounding gas vibrate like a violin string, proving the probe had entered interstellar space at eighteen billion kilometers out.

cut30Scenes.subtitle: 2026 TO 10 DECILLION YEARS // OUTLIVING THE STARS
cut30Scenes.headline: Two Sensors Awake Today, Gliding Beyond the Age of Stars
cut30Scenes.metricSub: Losing 4 watts/year, LECP shut down on April 17, 2026. Silent by the 2030s, Voyager 1 will outlast the Milky Way's stars.
cut30Scenes.summary: After engineers switched off another sensor in April 2026 to save fading plutonium heat, just two instruments remain awake. Long after its radio falls silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 will glide past alien stars and outlive the Milky Way itself.
cut30Scenes.voiceScript: With only two instruments awake after April 2026, Voyager 1 will fall silent in the 2030s. Yet its true voyage is just beginning. It will pass another star in forty thousand years, drift through the collision of the Milky Way and Andromeda, and outlive the stars themselves.
